storyTitle: As System Administrator, I want to perform access denial enforcement for unauthorized event requests to achieve security compliance

functional.title: Verify unauthorized API request to event endpoint returns HTTP 403 with generic error message
preconditions: Application is deployed and running in a test environment
A user account exists with a role that does NOT have permission to access event endpoints (e.g., role 'Viewer' or unauthenticated user)
API testing tool (e.g., Postman or cURL) is available
Event data exists in the application database

steps.action: Authenticate as a user without event access permissions (e.g., 'viewer_user') and obtain the session token or API key
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds and a valid session token is returned for the unauthorized role

steps.action: Send a GET request to the event endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events/123) using the unauthorized user's token in the Authorization header
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP status code 403 Forbidden

steps.action: Inspect the response body of the 403 response
steps.expectedResult: The response body contains a generic error message such as 'Access Denied' or 'You do not have permission to access this resource' and does NOT expose any event data, internal error details, stack traces, or system information

steps.action: Verify the response headers do not leak sensitive information (e.g., no X-Powered-By, no server version details)
steps.expectedResult: Response headers are clean and do not expose internal server technology or version information

steps.action: Check the application security/audit log for a record of this denied request
steps.expectedResult: An audit log entry is created recording the unauthorized access attempt including timestamp, user ID, requested resource, and the 403 response code

postconditions: No event data was returned or exposed to the unauthorized user
An audit log entry exists documenting the denied access attempt
The unauthorized user's session remains valid (they are not logged out) but access is still denied for protected resources

functional.title: Verify unauthorized API request to follow-up endpoint returns HTTP 403 with generic error message
preconditions: Application is deployed and running in a test environment
A user account exists with a role that does NOT have permission to access follow-up endpoints
Follow-up data exists in the application database linked to events
API testing tool is available

steps.action: Authenticate as a user without follow-up access permissions and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds and a valid session token is returned

steps.action: Send a GET request to the follow-up endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events/123/follow-ups) using the unauthorized user's token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP status code 403 Forbidden

steps.action: Send a POST request to create a follow-up (e.g., POST /api/events/123/follow-ups with a valid JSON body) using the unauthorized user's token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP status code 403 Forbidden with a generic error message

steps.action: Inspect both response bodies to confirm no follow-up or event data is leaked
steps.expectedResult: Both responses contain only a generic denial message and no follow-up data, event data, or internal system details are present

postconditions: No follow-up data was returned or created by the unauthorized user
Audit log entries exist for both denied access attempts
Existing follow-up data in the database remains unchanged

functional.title: Verify UI redirects unauthorized user to access-denied page without exposing event data
preconditions: Application is deployed and accessible via a web browser
A user account exists with a role that does NOT have permission to view events (e.g., 'basic_user')
Event data exists in the system that would be visible to authorized users
Browser developer tools are available for network inspection

steps.action: Open the application in a web browser and log in as 'basic_user' who does not have event access permissions
steps.expectedResult: User is logged in successfully and lands on the default dashboard or home page

steps.action: Manually navigate to the event listing page by entering the URL directly in the browser address bar (e.g., /events)
steps.expectedResult: The browser redirects the user to an access-denied page (e.g., /access-denied or /403)

steps.action: Inspect the access-denied page content
steps.expectedResult: The page displays a user-friendly message such as 'You do not have permission to access this page' with no event data, event IDs, event titles, or any sensitive information visible on the page

steps.action: Open browser developer tools and inspect the Network tab for the redirected request
steps.expectedResult: No event data was transferred in any network response; the redirect happened server-side or client-side before any event data was fetched

steps.action: View the page source of the access-denied page
steps.expectedResult: The HTML source contains no hidden event data, no event-related API responses embedded in scripts, and no sensitive information in comments or hidden elements

steps.action: Verify the access-denied page provides a navigation option (e.g., 'Go to Home' or 'Contact Administrator' link)
steps.expectedResult: The access-denied page includes at least one actionable link allowing the user to navigate back to an authorized area of the application

postconditions: User remains logged in but on the access-denied page
No event data was exposed at any point during the redirect flow
The user can navigate away from the access-denied page to authorized sections of the application

functional.title: Verify UI redirects unauthorized user accessing a specific event detail page to access-denied page
preconditions: Application is deployed and accessible via a web browser
A user account 'basic_user' exists without event access permissions
An event with ID 456 exists in the database with sensitive data
An authorized admin user has confirmed event 456 is visible when properly authorized

steps.action: Log in to the application as 'basic_user'
steps.expectedResult: User is logged in and sees the default home page

steps.action: Navigate directly to the event detail page by entering the URL /events/456 in the browser address bar
steps.expectedResult: The browser redirects the user to the access-denied page

steps.action: Verify the access-denied page does not display any details about event 456 (title, description, dates, participants)
steps.expectedResult: The access-denied page shows only a generic denial message with no reference to event 456 or its data

steps.action: Press the browser Back button
steps.expectedResult: The user is taken back to the previous authorized page, not to the event detail page

postconditions: Event 456 data was never rendered or exposed to the unauthorized user
An audit log entry records the unauthorized access attempt to event 456
User session remains active and functional for authorized pages

functional.title: Verify repeated unauthorized API attempts trigger a security alert notification
preconditions: Application is deployed with security alert notification system configured
A System Administrator account exists and is configured to receive security alert notifications (via email, dashboard, or SIEM integration)
The threshold for repeated unauthorized attempts is defined (e.g., 5 attempts within 10 minutes)
A user account 'attacker_user' exists without event access permissions
Security alert notification channel (email inbox, admin dashboard, or monitoring tool) is accessible for verification

steps.action: Authenticate as 'attacker_user' and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds and a valid session token is returned

steps.action: Send unauthorized API requests to the event endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events/1, GET /api/events/2, etc.) repeatedly, exceeding the configured threshold (e.g., send 6 requests within 2 minutes)
steps.expectedResult: Each request returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with a generic error message

steps.action: After exceeding the threshold, check the System Administrator's notification channel (email inbox, admin dashboard alerts section, or SIEM tool)
steps.expectedResult: A security alert notification has been generated and delivered, indicating repeated unauthorized access attempts from 'attacker_user'

steps.action: Inspect the security alert notification content
steps.expectedResult: The notification includes: the user identifier (attacker_user), the number of unauthorized attempts, the time window, the targeted endpoints, and a timestamp of the alert

steps.action: Verify the alert is visible in the application's security/admin dashboard if applicable
steps.expectedResult: The security alert appears in the admin dashboard's alerts or notifications section with appropriate severity level (e.g., 'Warning' or 'Critical')

postconditions: A security alert notification was successfully delivered to the System Administrator
All unauthorized attempts are logged individually in the audit log
The attacker_user's session may or may not be invalidated depending on security policy, but the alert has been raised
The security alert is persisted and can be reviewed later by administrators

functional.title: Verify authorized user can successfully access event endpoints without denial
preconditions: Application is deployed and running
A user account 'admin_user' exists with System Administrator role and full event access permissions
Event data exists in the database (e.g., event ID 100 with known title 'Annual Review Meeting')
API testing tool is available

steps.action: Authenticate as 'admin_user' with System Administrator role and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds and a valid session token with admin privileges is returned

steps.action: Send a GET request to the event listing endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events) using the admin token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 200 OK with a list of events including event ID 100

steps.action: Send a GET request to a specific event detail endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events/100) using the admin token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 200 OK with full event details including title 'Annual Review Meeting', description, dates, and all associated data

steps.action: Send a GET request to the follow-up endpoint (e.g., GET /api/events/100/follow-ups) using the admin token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 200 OK with follow-up data associated with event 100

steps.action: Verify no security alert was triggered for these authorized requests
steps.expectedResult: No security alert notification is generated for the authorized admin user's requests

postconditions: Authorized user received full event and follow-up data as expected
No false-positive security alerts were generated
Audit log records the successful authorized access for traceability

functional.title: Verify authorized user can access events via UI without being redirected to access-denied page

A user account 'admin_user' exists with System Administrator role

steps.action: Verify at no point during navigation was the user redirected to an access-denied page
steps.expectedResult: All pages loaded successfully without any access-denied redirects or 403 errors

postconditions: Admin user successfully viewed all event and follow-up data
No access-denied pages were encountered during the entire flow
User remains logged in with full admin session active

functional.title: Verify security alert notification contains actionable information for System Administrator
preconditions: Application is deployed with security alert system configured
System Administrator 'admin_user' is configured to receive security alerts
The repeated unauthorized attempt threshold has been previously triggered (from TC-FUNC-005 or equivalent)

steps.action: Log in as 'admin_user' with System Administrator role
steps.expectedResult: Admin user is logged in and sees the admin dashboard

steps.action: Navigate to the security alerts or notifications section of the admin dashboard
steps.expectedResult: The security alerts section loads and displays recent alerts including the one triggered by repeated unauthorized attempts

steps.action: Click on the security alert to view its full details
steps.expectedResult: The alert detail view shows: offending user ID/username, IP address (if available), number of attempts, time range of attempts, targeted endpoints/resources, and severity level

steps.action: Verify the alert provides options for the administrator to take action (e.g., 'Block User', 'Investigate', 'Dismiss')
steps.expectedResult: The alert detail view includes actionable buttons or links allowing the administrator to respond to the security incident

postconditions: System Administrator was able to review the full security alert details
The alert contains sufficient information for incident investigation
The alert status can be updated (e.g., acknowledged, resolved) by the administrator

functional.title: Verify access denial enforcement works correctly for different HTTP methods on event endpoints
preconditions: Application is deployed and running
A user account 'unauthorized_user' exists without event access permissions
Event with ID 100 exists in the database
API testing tool is available

steps.action: Authenticate as 'unauthorized_user' and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds and a valid session token is returned

steps.action: Send a GET request to GET /api/events/100 using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned with a generic error message

steps.action: Send a POST request to POST /api/events with a valid event JSON body using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned with a generic error message; no event is created

steps.action: Send a PUT request to PUT /api/events/100 with modified event data using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned with a generic error message; event 100 data remains unchanged

steps.action: Send a DELETE request to DELETE /api/events/100 using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned with a generic error message; event 100 still exists in the database

steps.action: Verify event 100 data is unchanged by querying the database or using an authorized account
steps.expectedResult: Event 100 exists with all original data intact, confirming no unauthorized modifications occurred

postconditions: All HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) were properly blocked for the unauthorized user
No data was created, modified, or deleted by the unauthorized requests
All denied attempts are recorded in the audit log

functional.title: Verify access denial enforcement differentiates between multiple user roles correctly
preconditions: Application is deployed and running
Three user accounts exist: 'admin_user' (System Administrator with full access), 'event_viewer' (read-only event access), and 'no_access_user' (no event permissions)
Events and follow-ups exist in the database
API testing tool is available

steps.action: Authenticate as 'no_access_user' and send GET /api/events
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned with a generic error message

steps.action: Authenticate as 'event_viewer' and send GET /api/events
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 200 OK is returned with event listing data (read-only access granted)

steps.action: As 'event_viewer', send POST /api/events with a new event body
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned because event_viewer has read-only access, not create permissions

steps.action: Authenticate as 'admin_user' and send POST /api/events with a new event body
steps.expectedResult: HTTP 201 Created is returned and the new event is successfully created

steps.action: Verify audit logs show appropriate access decisions for each role
steps.expectedResult: Audit logs show 403 for no_access_user on GET, 200 for event_viewer on GET, 403 for event_viewer on POST, and 201 for admin_user on POST

postconditions: Role-based access control correctly differentiated between three permission levels
Only the admin_user was able to create a new event
Audit logs accurately reflect all access decisions per role

steps.action: Send a POST request to /api/events with a valid JSON body but no Authorization header

steps.action: Inspect all response bodies to confirm no sensitive data leakage
steps.expectedResult: All responses contain only generic error messages with no event data, stack traces, or internal system details

negative.title: Verify API request with expired authentication token is denied

API testing tool is available
Event data exists in the database

steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden with a generic error message indicating the session has expired or is invalid

negative.title: Verify API request with tampered/forged authentication token is denied

A forged or tampered JWT token has been crafted (e.g., modified payload with admin role but invalid signature)

Event data exists in the database

steps.expectedResult: Token is crafted and ready for use

steps.action: Send a GET request to /api/events using the tampered token in the Authorization header

steps.action: Send a DELETE request to /api/events/100 using the tampered token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 401 or 403 and event 100 is NOT deleted

steps.action: Verify event 100 still exists by querying with a valid authorized token
steps.expectedResult: Event 100 exists with all data intact, confirming the tampered token had no effect

postconditions: The tampered token was rejected and no access was granted

The tampered token attempt is logged as a security event in the audit log

negative.title: Verify SQL injection in event ID parameter does not bypass access control
preconditions: Application is deployed and running
A user account 'unauthorized_user' exists without event access permissions
API testing tool is available
Database contains event data

steps.action: Authenticate as 'unauthorized_user' and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds

steps.action: Send a GET request to /api/events/1%20OR%201=1 (SQL injection in event ID) using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 400 Bad Request; no event data is returned

steps.action: Send a GET request to /api/events/1'; DROP TABLE events;-- using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 403 or 400; no SQL injection is executed and no data is affected

steps.action: Send a GET request to /api/events/1 UNION SELECT * FROM users-- using the unauthorized token
steps.expectedResult: The API returns HTTP 403 or 400 with a generic error message; no user data or event data is leaked

steps.action: Verify the events table and data are intact by querying with an authorized admin account
steps.expectedResult: All event data is intact and the events table exists with no corruption

postconditions: No SQL injection was executed against the database
All event data remains intact and uncorrupted
The injection attempts are logged in the security audit log
Access control was enforced before any query execution

negative.title: Verify unauthorized user cannot bypass access control by changing HTTP method
preconditions: Application is deployed and running
A user account 'unauthorized_user' exists without event access permissions
API testing tool is available
Event with ID 100 exists in the database

steps.action: Authenticate as 'unauthorized_user' and obtain the session token
steps.expectedResult: Authentication succeeds

postconditions: Error message is announced by screen readers automatically on page load
ARIA live region is properly implemented with correct politeness level
Error message is not hidden from assistive technology
The implementation follows WAI-ARIA 1.1 best practices for alert messages

accessibility.title: Verify access-denied page has proper focus management when user is redirected from an event page
preconditions: User is not authenticated
User attempts to access a protected event URL directly
Screen reader is active (optional but recommended)
Browser is Chrome, Firefox, or Edge

steps.action: Navigate directly to /events/1 in the browser address bar while not authenticated
steps.expectedResult: User is redirected to the access-denied page

steps.action: Immediately after the access-denied page loads, check where the keyboard focus is placed (press Tab once and observe which element receives focus)
steps.expectedResult: Focus is placed on the main heading ('Access Denied') or the first meaningful content element on the page — NOT on a random element in the header/footer or lost in the body. Alternatively, focus is on the page's <main> element with tabindex='-1'

steps.action: Verify that the focus placement is visible (a focus ring or outline is shown on the focused element)
steps.expectedResult: A visible focus indicator is present on the element that received initial focus. The indicator meets the 3:1 contrast requirement

steps.action: Press Tab to move to the next interactive element
steps.expectedResult: Focus moves to the first actionable element (e.g., 'Go to Login' link). The transition is smooth with no focus jumping to unexpected locations

steps.action: Press Escape key on the access-denied page
steps.expectedResult: No unexpected behavior occurs. If a modal or dialog is present, it closes. If no modal, Escape has no adverse effect. Focus is not lost

steps.action: Use browser DevTools to verify that the focused element on page load has an appropriate tabindex or is a naturally focusable element
steps.expectedResult: The initially focused element either has tabindex='-1' (for programmatic focus) or is a naturally focusable element like a heading with tabindex='-1'. No positive tabindex values (tabindex='1', '2', etc.) are used anywhere on the page

postconditions: Focus is managed correctly on redirect to access-denied page
No focus traps or lost focus states exist
Focus order is logical and predictable
No positive tabindex values disrupt the natural tab order

accessibility.title: Verify access-denied page is accessible on mobile devices with touch and gesture support
preconditions: Mobile device (iOS or Android) with screen reader available (VoiceOver on iOS, TalkBack on Android)
User is not authenticated
Mobile browser (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android) is open
Device is in portrait orientation

steps.action: On the mobile device, navigate to /events/1 in the mobile browser while not authenticated
steps.expectedResult: User is redirected to the access-denied page. Page renders correctly in mobile viewport without horizontal scrolling

steps.action: Verify that all touch targets (links, buttons) have a minimum size of 44x44 CSS pixels
steps.expectedResult: All interactive elements ('Go to Login' link/button, any other links) have touch targets of at least 44x44 pixels. Elements are not too close together (at least 8px spacing)

steps.action: Enable VoiceOver (iOS) or TalkBack (Android) and swipe right to navigate through page elements
steps.expectedResult: Screen reader navigates through all elements in logical order: heading, error message, navigation links. Each element is announced with its role and label

steps.action: Double-tap on the 'Go to Login' link when it is focused by the screen reader
steps.expectedResult: The link is activated and user is navigated to the login page. The action works identically to a single tap for sighted users

steps.action: Rotate the device to landscape orientation
steps.expectedResult: Page content reflows appropriately. No content is lost or hidden. All interactive elements remain accessible and properly sized

steps.action: Pinch to zoom on the access-denied page
steps.expectedResult: Zoom is not disabled (no maximum-scale=1 or user-scalable=no in viewport meta tag). Content scales properly when zoomed

postconditions: Access-denied page is fully functional on mobile devices
All touch targets meet minimum size requirements
Screen reader navigation works correctly on mobile
Zoom is not restricted and content scales properly

userStoryObject.title: As System Administrator, I want to perform access denial enforcement for unauthorized event requests to achieve security compliance
userStoryObject.description:
CONTEXT & BACKGROUND:
The system must block and gracefully handle any unauthorized attempt to access event or follow-up endpoints.

CURRENT STATE:
Manual or incomplete process today.

DESIRED STATE:
System supports the capability end-to-end.

KEY FUNCTIONALITY:
• Implement core logic and validation
• Expose API and UI
• Handle errors and edge cases
• Ensure data persistence and retrieval

USER INTERACTION FLOW:
1. User accesses the feature
2. User performs the required action
3. System processes the request
4. System displays results or confirmation
5. User verifies the outcome

TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:
• Data source: application database
• Security: authentication and input validation
• Performance: meet SLA requirements

OUT OF SCOPE:
• Advanced customization (future story)

SUCCESS METRICS:
• Feature works per acceptance criteria
• No critical defects in production

**Persona:** System Administrator

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Unauthorized API requests return HTTP 403 with a generic error message
2. UI redirects unauthorized users to an access-denied page without exposing event data
3. Repeated unauthorized attempts trigger a security alert notification
4. System handles the operation correctly and returns expected results for scenario 4
5. System handles the operation correctly and returns expected results for scenario 5
